newsitem.title: USA: MTBE slightly up on unleaded's strength.
newsitem.headline: MTBE slightly up on unleaded's strength.

text.p: U.S. spot MTBE prices gained ground late this week amid stronger unleaded gasoline values but the market still risked bearish moves due to imports, players said on Thursday.
Trade, however, remained light with only a few deals slipping through. "The market is not doing anything. It's pretty thin," said a New York Harbor trader.

Prompt MTBE in Houston was about a cent higher than a week ago at about 75.75 cents gallon, staying within the weak 13 cent to 15 cent differential to NYMEX unleaded. That differential compares to more than 20 cents two years ago, in the more bullish days when RFG was launched.

In New York Harbor, spot MTBE was widely ranged at 79.25/80.75 cents. A 20,000-deal in the Harbor for 79.50 cents was done Wednesday and a 50,00-barrel parcel for 80.00 cents for the second half of May was sold earlier Thursday.
Traders said a very prompt parcel fob was done at 80.75 cents.
Some players said the market may weaken under the weight of MTBE imports and a tick up in worldwide production.

Traders said new supplies were entering the market following the start up of a 50,00 tonne-per-year plant in Singapore as part of the Singapore $3.4 billion petrochemical complex which started producing on specification ethylene early last week.
Meanwhile, Arco's MTBE unit in California was heard back up following an unscheduled turnaround last month and Huntsman was rumored having production problems. Neither could be immediately confirmed.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
